customer.business: Parity (free, open-source behavior proof for software changes)
customer.target: People who change or replace software they did not write and need to know nothing broke: developers using AI coding agents, IT service providers migrating old business apps, and owners of an old business app
customer.where: Online, worldwide; found on GitHub, Hacker News, Reddit, X, dev newsletters

segments.name: Developer in a product team that uses AI coding agents daily
Solo developer or freelancer maintaining client apps
Consultant at an IT services firm doing legacy migrations
Owner or office manager of a small business running an old Windows app
IT staff in a public body (city, hospital, school district)

behaviours.name: Tries new GitHub tools
behaviours.how: Stars repos weekly, installs a CLI if the README convinces them in a minute.

behaviours.name: Skeptical of AI tools
behaviours.how: Has been burned by AI hype; wants proof on their own code before trusting anything.

behaviours.name: Already has a test suite
behaviours.how: Relies on unit and end-to-end tests and CI; adds tools only when tests miss something painful.

behaviours.name: Firefighter with no time
behaviours.how: Too busy to set anything up; adopts only what works in under an hour.

behaviours.name: Needs approval to adopt
behaviours.how: Has to justify any new tool to a manager, security team or procurement.

behaviours.name: Non-technical, relies on a provider
behaviours.how: Does not install tools; would use it only if their IT provider or a simple app does it for them.

pitch:
Parity: proof that your software still does the same thing after a change.
Record your app in use once (a screen recording, optionally narrated). Parity explores the rest on its own in a sandbox and writes the business rules it found in plain language for you to confirm.
After any change (a refactor by an AI coding agent, a framework upgrade, a full rewrite of an old app), Parity replays the same scenarios on the old and new versions and shows every field that differs, with the evidence.
Works on web apps and old Windows apps. Uses Meta's AI models to capture and explain; the replays themselves run without AI.
Free and open source on GitHub. Runs on your machine.
